challenge.situations.md:
# Archive situations

All three situations extend `archive-one` in [cases.jsonl](cases.jsonl). The [owner decision](owner.md) defines the archive behavior.

## ARC-01 · Archive two of four notes — supported

Start with A, B, C and D active. Select A and C, then archive once. B and D must each remain active once, and neither selected note may remain active. Both `["B","D"]` and `["D","B"]` satisfy the owner's rule.

The singleton selects every active note. A generator that always clears the active list and one that archives only the first selected note would therefore both pass. On the proposed input, the former would lose B and D (`[]`), while the latter would leave C active (`["B","C","D"]`). These are hypothetical outcomes.

Running `python3 grade.py archive-one '[]'` returned `True`. Supplying `["A"]`, `["B","D"]` or `["D","B"]` returned `False` in each trial. The existing row can detect A staying active, but it has no surviving note to check. Those scores apply only to the singleton.

## ARC-02 · Require a fixed display order — rejected

With the ARC-01 selection, reverse the display of the two survivors. Requiring B before D would penalize a valid user preference. Accept either permutation under ARC-01. The owner explicitly leaves display order to the user, and [grade.py](grade.py) compares sorted lists.

## ARC-03 · Archive the same notes again — open

After ARC-01, issue a second archive request naming A and C while both are already archived. The owner marks repeat archive undecided. Should the second request succeed as a no-op, report that the notes are already archived, or produce another observable result? B and D are still unselected and must stay active. Their survival alone cannot decide the required response to the repeat request.

## Handoff

Create Eval can take ARC-01 from this index and append its row ID and control results to [release-history.tsv](release-history.tsv). Use both survivor orders as valid controls and both hypothetical failures above as negative controls. ARC-02 records the reason to omit an order requirement. Bootstrap can take ARC-03 to the owner before repeat archive receives a score.

correct.situations.md:
# Archive situations

The [owner correction](owner.md) sets the boundary at two selected notes. The existing [eval rows](cases.jsonl) cover one selection and a pair. The controls below used synthetic active-note lists as the final argument to `python3 grade.py ROW_ID`.

## ARC-01 · Preview two of four notes — supported

Start with A, B, C and D active. Select A and C and invoke Archive once. Archive previews the selection and all four notes must remain active exactly once. Row `ARC-01` checks the resulting active list. The grader has no input for the visible preview.

| Row | Grader returned True | Grader returned False |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `archive-one` (only A active and selected) | `[]` | `["A"]`, `["B","D"]`, `["D","B"]` |
| `ARC-01` (A and C selected) | `["A","B","C","D"]`, `["D","C","B","A"]` | `["B","D"]`, `["D","B"]`, `[]`, `["B","C","D"]`, `["B","D","D"]`, `["A","C","D"]`, `["A","B","C","D","D"]` |

The original ARC-01 expectation archived A and C. Its control results appear in entry 5 of [release-history.tsv](release-history.tsv). Entry 6 supersedes that expectation for the same input.

## ARC-02 · Require a fixed display order — rejected

Display order remains a user preference. Both four-note orders above pass ARC-01. There is no separate scored row for order.

## ARC-03 · Archive the same notes again — open

Invoking Archive twice after selecting A and C starts the second invocation with all four notes still active. The owner has left repeat behavior undecided. ARC-03 stays outside scoring pending an owner decision.

audit.audit/arc-01/review.md:
# ARC-01 release scoring review · 2026-11-16

Before inspecting the scorers: owner.md's correction and ledger entry 6 supersede entries 1, 2 and 5 for multi-selection. Starting active [A,B,C,D], selecting A and C and invoking Archive once must leave each of A,B,C,D active once. Reversing display order is valid (ARC-02 rejected a fixed order); leaving only B,D is wrong. A single selected A still archives. ARC-03 (repeat) is undecided and excluded. The active list does not establish that a preview was displayed.

The release scorer gave a false pass. From the project root, run:

    python3 release_grade.py ARC-01 '["A","B","D","D"]'

It printed True. Replacing C with a second D changes just one entry and keeps the length at four. Release checks length alone. Replacing D with an unknown X also passed. The previous grader (grade.py) rejected both lists: it compares sorted identities, preserving duplicate counts while ignoring order. Both graders accepted the unchanged list and its reverse. Both rejected the superseded two-survivor result. All entry 6 controls agreed across graders: each of its invalid ARC-01 lists has the wrong length, so none distinguishes counting from checking identities. The single-selection control still accepted [] and rejected ["A"].

[Raw replay](replay.jsonl) contains every argument vector, complete submitted list, stdout, stderr and exit code. Each local Python CLI invocation began in a fresh process reading unchanged cases.jsonl from the project root. [SHA-256 manifest](inputs.sha256) pins the sources and ledger **before** the audit entry. All hashes matched after replay. This was an operator-run development audit using only the result argument; no candidate ran, no application state was observed, and no isolation or candidate discovery is claimed. One operator chose the wrong result and the legitimate controls. Independent intent review: **unreviewed** (reviewer unavailable).

Next decision — release owner: hold ARC-01 release passes as evidence of note preservation. Decide whether to require a JSON list with exactly the expected note IDs and counts in any order and to retain the same-length substitution alongside the reverse-order control. Create Eval can use the existing grade.py comparison as a reference for note lists. The comparison rejected both substitutions and accepted the reverse on replay; no release repair was implemented or validated. If authorized, replay these controls on the actual release entry point and obtain independent review before adoption. Visible preview would need its own observation; ARC-03 remains with the owner. No grader, case or skill change proposed here has been adopted.
